Descriptions.ShortDescription: Sends every frame NINA saves to your Bortle, which develops the night when the sequence ends.
Descriptions.LongDescription:
Delivers your frames to Bortle (bortle.eu or your own install) while you image.

- Every frame NINA saves is uploaded in the background. A queue on disk keeps
  them through network loss and restarts; nothing is ever deleted on this PC.
  Each NINA profile, server and key has its own queue: frames go only to the
  account they were captured for, and switching uploads off holds the queue.
- When the sequence ends, Bortle develops all nights of that target together,
  on the level you chose when planning (step by step, guarded, or automatic).
- The "Finish Bortle session" instruction, placed last in the End area after
  parking, waits for the last frames and reports the end. Without it, the end
  of the sequence does the same.
- The "Bortle Livestream" panel (imaging tab) streams the night to YouTube
  with one button. Bortle makes the stream on its server from the uploaded
  frames; this PC sends no video.

The plugin only delivers data. It controls no equipment and never delays or
fails a sequence; safety stays with NINA.

Bortle.eu is in private beta: request access at https://bortle.eu
("Zugang beantragen"), or run your own install (open source). Then create
the plugin key in Bortle under Profil → NINA-Plugin.

Open source under the AGPL-3.0. Written with substantial help from an AI model
(Anthropic's Claude) and maintained by Benjamin Hartwich; see the repository's
README for what that means.
